n1.text:
Status: proposed. Amended 2026-09-24: all map-relative sizes, positions, offsets and spacing are in map units (1,000 on the longest edge), converted from the pixel draft at the recovered map's scale. Asset image dimensions stay in pixels.

These are interface drawings, not evidence that anything works. No size, count or duration here has been measured, and the sample data is invented: Aethermoor — West Reaches, the Aethermoor Starter pack 0.4.2, the pine-highland and ridge-peak families. The 238 stamps and 7,559 x 8,192 source figures come from the specification's own fixture observations.

Built on Phase 1's shell and tokens unchanged. Additions are listed on the Control matrix.

n2.text:
The one idea the whole phase turns on:

three different things are called "size", and they must never share a panel.

library defaults - what a future placement starts from, shared across projects, no undo step.

next stamp - the Stamp tool's own state, what the ghost shows, carried across asset changes.

on the map - a placement that exists; every edit is a document command.

Each panel header carries its tag. See the Targets frame.

n3.text:
Scatter, precisely:

spacing is an AVERAGE centre-to-centre distance in map units - not a minimum distance, not a collision solver, not a percentage of stamp size, and unaffected by zoom or by editing and export resolution.

Size and rotation ranges switch on independently. Random flip, tint and opacity are not offered: they were considered and left out, so there is no disabled row pretending otherwise.

Committed placements are resolved and stored. Nothing re-randomises them - not reopening, not export, not a future algorithm. Only Re-roll, which is its own command.

n4.text:
Multi-selection, the mixed rule:

SCALING resizes each stamp about its own anchor. A forest gets bigger trees, not a spread-out forest.

ROTATION turns the arrangement about one shared centre - proposed as the bounding-box centre of the unlocked selection, fixed when the drag starts so it cannot drift.

Locked objects are excluded from both, and from the shared centre, and the selection count says so rather than silently skipping them.

n5.text:
Open questions for engineering, in DESIGN-RESPONSE §12:

every bound marked P on the Control matrix; the shared rotation-centre convention; hit-cycle wrap feedback; the five-category vocabulary; scatter asset weighting; the 180 ms search debounce; the 4 map-unit duplicate offset; whether the keyboard nudge steps in screen pixels (zoom-relative) or map units (fixed); whether nonuniform scale should be refused at edit time rather than at export preflight.
